summary: Intermittent p99 timeouts from continuous-batcher 'linger' growth under mixed short/long traffic
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent p99 end-to-end request timeouts (504) during normal production traffic. Impact: High — ClarifyAI observed user-facing errors impacting chat sessions during peak trading hours for their app. Environment: Dedicated capacity in us-east-1, customer pinned to redwood-rlhf-v1 and occasionally fallback to meta-llama-2-70b-chat. Observed behavior: p50/p90 steady, p95 elevated briefly, p99 spikes to 3-6s and occasional 504s. Spikes correlate with periods of mixed short (10-20 tokens) and long (400-800 tokens) requests from the same connection pool. Initial report included logs showing batcher flush delays and request linger values climbing prior to timeouts.
steps_to_reproduce: Send a sustained mixed QPS pattern: burst of short prompts (10–20 tokens) followed by sporadic long completions (400–800 tokens) from multiple clients hitting the same model pool.
Observe latency percentiles in the console per-route for 10–30 minutes.
Replay captured traffic through canary environment with batcher tracing enabled (see attached trace IDs in logs).
Toggle continuous_batching feature flag to reproduce delta in latency profiles.
investigation_notes: 03/10 14:20 — Support reproduced p99 spike in staging when replaying mixed-length traffic; enabling batcher tracing reveals linger growth from ~20ms to ~250ms within 30s windows.

03/10 15:05 — Hypothesis: continuous-batcher increases linger/window when per-connection QPS drops; mixed long requests block KV cache priming and cause the coalescer to wait for larger windows to reach target batch size.

03/10 16:30 — Correlated spike windows with KV cache eviction events; when cache miss rate rose, token generation for long requests increased worker occupancy, reducing effective QPS for short requests which in turn grew linger_ms.
03/11 09:10 — Load test: setting batcher config max_linger_ms=50 eliminated p99 spikes; setting min_batch_size to 1 reduced p50 slightly but stabilized tail.
03/11 11:30 — Deployment note: customer is on a dedicated pool with autoscaling disabled; observed that pool sizing < expected contributed to higher worker saturation during long generations.
03/12 10:00 — Eng spike analysis (PR referenced) suggests adding a passive-reset mechanism that forces the batcher to shrink its effective linger after a long request completes on the pool.
Instrumentation added: per-request batcher_linger_ms metrics and connection-level occupancy counters (enabled in canary).
comments: 2026-03-10 15:00 — Clara (Support): Received initial customer logs. Marking as P1 due to user-facing errors. Escalated to SRE.
2026-03-10 15:12 — Omar (SRE): Reproduced in staging. Tracing indicates continuous-batcher linger growth. Added traces to ticket.
2026-03-11 09:45 — Aisha (Customer): Confirmed that after lowering max_linger_ms in our canary the errors stopped; customer requests a short-term mitigation on prod.
2026-03-11 12:05 — Omar (SRE): Pushed mitigation to ClarifyAI pool: set max_linger_ms=60 and min_batch_size=1 for their dedicated pool. Monitoring.

2026-03-12 08:20 — Dev (Runtime): Proposed permanent fix in PR 1284 to reset linger_on_idle and add logic to prioritize short-request flush when mixed workloads detected. Planning rollout to canary tomorrow.
resolution: Mitigation applied: decreased continuous-batcher max_linger_ms to 60ms and reduced min_batch_size to 1 for ClarifyAI dedicated pool which eliminated observed p99 spikes. Follow-up: runtime PR#1284 to implement passive linger reset and short-request prioritization scheduled for canary on 2026-03-15 and prod rollout pending validation. Customer advised to increase pool size or enable autoscaling as longer-term operational recommendation. Postmortem and runbook updates scheduled (see related_confluence_pages).
